title: Bounded guard computation on one tape
statement: Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $i$ be one of the $k$ work tapes, and let $F$ be a machine format. Let $x$, $bits$, and $rest$ be Boolean words such that paired decoding of $x$ yields $(bits,rest)$. Set $B=\max\{F.guard,(4F.k+5)3^{F.k+1}\}$, and let $d$ be a configuration on input $x$ whose state is the running decrement phase, whose input head is at $2|bits|+3$, whose tape $i$ stores the word obtained by applying fixed-width increment to $bits$ with a zero appended (using the empty word if increment overflows), whose head on tape $i$ is at $0$, and whose output is empty. When the guard counter machine with block size $B$ is embedded on tape $i$ and run from $d$, there is a time $t\le (B+6)(|x|+1)$ at which its state is done if $B(\operatorname{value}(bits)+1)\le |rest|$, and escape otherwise; its output is empty and its input head is respectively at $2|bits|+3+B(\operatorname{value}(bits)+1)$ or $|x|+1$. At every earlier time $u<t$ its state is neither done nor escape, and every tape other than $i$ and its head position are unchanged from $d$.
